newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses on Dow after slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses on Dow after slow trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks recovered partially in late trade on Tuesday from their early slide, but the bourse closed down for the first time in five sessions on lack of foreign investor interest, traders and analysts said.
Key blue chips rebounded with the U.S. Dow Jones Industrial Average late in the session, traders said.

"The Dow recovered towards the close and that promptly revived a few stocks," said Gerardo Copca, associate director of research at the Finamex brokerage. The leading IPC share index ended down 8.61 points, or 0.23 percent, at 3,784.22.
Trading volume was dull at 42.7 million shares.

"The market, however, is still awaiting developments in U.S. interest rates and Q1 domestic corporate earnings. Volume is slow as brokers are switching stocks and there are no foreign investors in the market," Copca added.
A floor trader noted market forecast that an increase in domestic interest rates was imminent, but said volume was low due to investor caution on lack of a fixed market trend.
"If volume were heavier, then I would say no, they don't like the upcoming hike in (Cetes) rates, but it isn't and foreigners are nowhere to be seen," he said.
"I think they're staying out because many are invested and the opportunity cost of buying or selling is too high until we know which way the bourse is headed," he added.

A Reuters survey of money market dealers showed they forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 22.66 percent at its weekly auction to be held later in the day. This would be a rise of 80 basis points since last week. Auction results are due at 1830 local time/2330 GMT. Traders noted that Alfa, Grupo Carso and Cemex had all staged late recoveries that helped the IPC to rebound from a low of 3,764.63 points.
Industrial conglomerate Alfa A shares rose 1.25 pesos at 45.25 pesos, cement makers Cemex CPO gained 35 centavos to 29.00 pesos, while holding company Grupo Carso edged up 15 centavos to 46.45 pesos.
Telecoms firm Telmex, down 18 centavos at 15.78 pesos and financial group GFB, which declined three centavos to 2.77 pesos, weighed most on the downside, traders said.
The two stocks together accounted for 30 percent of all shares traded during the session.
Like its counterpart GFB, financial stock Banacci ended down, off 10 centavos to 18.40 pesos.
"GFB and Banacci are clearly sensitive to Cetes rates," said Robert Lacoursiere, a banking sector analyst at Santander Investment.
The broad market scoreboard shadowed performance by blue chips, with decliners outnumbering gainers by 51 to 28.
Situr, tourist arm of the debt-ridden Sidek group was a prominent percentage decliner, down one centavo to 24 centavos.
Dealers noted retail group Salinas y Rocha, up five centavos to 60 centavos, was near the head of the prominent gainers' list for the third day in a row.
"There are rumours the group is for sale. It is worse off than Sears (de Mexico) was. The share price settled in the deal will be very interesting," a trader said.
Sears Roebuck Co last week sold a 60-percent stake in its Mexican subsidiary to Grupo Carso.
Dealers noted El Puerto de Liverpool, another retail group, was also a leading gainer, up 20 centavos to 7.60 pesos.
